I rented a vehicle from enterprise while my car was being repaired.  I rented the vehicle from June 8th- 12th. When I returned the rental the car was signed off from any damage.  Then about 6 weeks later I received a letter demanding money for damage to the vehicle. I went over to enterprise in Galesburg, Il where I  rented the vehicle from. I was told that if the claim was under 1000 then they wouldn't presume it. I was given a claim number and phone number to contact the claims department.  When I called I was told there wasn't anything under my name or claim number. I thought that would be the end of it. This past Friday I received a text and phone number about the same claim number. I was told I did damage the car and now they say I damaged the carpet as well. I google this phone number 866-3004407. It states this is a scam claiming damage was done to a vehicle rented from enterprise.

I ordered 2 jackets from OliverandBlake from a Facebook advertisement., which then rerouted me to the OliverBlakeCompany website. I was contacted via email after 3 days by the company saying  the product was delayed and they gave me a discount code (DELAY25) to make additional purchases as a compensation for the delay. The tracking was from China and NOT the USA or London (where it is based supposedly). Tracking showed the order going to Chicago (ORD). Then a few days later all the tracking from the tracking number disappeared. 3 weeks later, no product was delivered and all tracking disappeared. This seems to be a ghost website scam generated through Facebook to lure people to make a purchase, then gives a fake tracking site and then doesn't deliver. I performed a chargeback dispute and cancelled my credit card.

I was targeted in a YouTube ad for a service that supposedly allows you to compare various car insurance quotes to locate the cheapest one. I entered mine and my husband's information but at the end of the form submission was not provided with actual quotes, but rather just links to various insurers to then have to fill out another form for an insurance quote on the insurer's website, which I could've just done to begin with without needing this third party provider.
Since submitting our information, my husband's phone and email have been blowing up incessantly with solicitation from every single insurer imaginable, with some of them calling multiple times in a row without us having explicitly given consent to each insurer to be contacted. This third-party provider just sold our information to these insurers without actually delivering the insights they were advertising. Effectively, it was false advertising and very frustrating to now be bombarded with solicitation attempts.

It has come to our attention that your company is actively using the intellectual property, registered logos, and graphics of Mississippi Mud Coffee, INC. without authorization. Specifically, you are advertising and selling unauthorized "5 lb bags" under our proprietary brand names, including "Mississippi Mud Coffee" and "Dancing Dogs Coffee."Our customers have notified us that your website is charging inflated prices for these items, printing counterfeit labels, and either failing to fulfill the orders or filling our branded bags with cheap, inferior substitute coffee. This unauthorized use of our corporate name, trademarks, and trade dress constitutes clear trademark infringement, unfair competition, and consumer fraud under federal and state laws. Your actions are causing severe, irreparable harm to our brand reputation and defrauding the public. We demand that you immediately take the following actions:
Christopher Ruess, President, Founder, Mississippi Mud Coffee
